title: Uniform
logline: Branch B, the first hour after the vote: Nandini pushes Nirala's wrists down instead of cuffing them, knowing whose name the DSP will write. She dresses him as an officer of her own force, takes his medal as a promise, buttons the wooden revolver into its holster and wires him with her own phone on an open call to Pushpa's handset, where the recording is kept. He walks alone into Bhaiyaji's godown and does the job aloud, until he reads the slip: the SHO has already signed it. Bhaiyaji laughs. He was waiting for a fake inspector. Then he finds the phone.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; names, 'madam', 'ji' and 'sahab' kept as spoken in India.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, six weeks into her first posting at the Imlipur thana. Tonight she breaks the DSP's order on her own word and sends an unarmed impostor in to get Bhaiyaji on tape.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves buttoned at the wrist; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars each; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip (the cuffs go back into it in b1 and stay there); black shoes; blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no name tag, no stars. From b3 shot 3 to the end, Nirala's brass medal is inside her buttoned left chest pocket, out of sight (the pen stays clipped on it until she takes it out in b7). Her black smartphone is in her right chest pocket from b1; she takes it out off frame in b5 shot 1 to dial Pushpa. From b5 she has no phone: hers is in his pocket. A small pocket notebook with a plain dark cover is in her left trouser pocket, out of sight, from b1 to b6; from b7 shot 1 it is already out, open on her knee (b7 to b10); her right trouser pocket holds the memo pad used in s2b02. Cherry-red open-face helmet under her left arm outdoors (b6); on the stall bench beside her in b7 to b11, where she leaves it.
characters.voice_note: Same actor and voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral, educated small-city north-Indian accent: not British, not American. Keeps 'madam', 'ji' and 'sahab' as Indians say them. Quick and clipped by habit, but tonight she is under pressure from the first line, so she is quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic. In b5 she gives orders like a checklist. At the stall she speaks three times: l22 is a murmur as she writes; l25 and l31 are low and level, said to herself, and must be fully clear. In b2 (l28) and b4 (l07) she speaks over her own hands at work: plain, practical, not tender.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: The self-appointed 'Inspector' of the fake thana. Tonight Nandini sends him to Bhaiyaji's godown, alone, as the 'Inspector sahab' Bhaiyaji thinks he bought.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, a neat black pencil moustache, clean-shaven chin. Home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched, ONE SIZE TOO BIG; teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES: khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge, worn dead level. Brown leather holster with a buttoned flap on his right hip. PERIOD 1 in b1: shoulder seams drooping, sleeves over his knuckles, belt tail hanging loose, the brass medal (blank brass-yellow disc as wide as a palm on a broad maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon) pinned above his left chest pocket. b2 changes him one item per still: belt tight and tail tucked, then shoulder seams squared, then cuffs folded back so his hands show; the medal is still on him through b2 and b3 shot 1. PERIOD 1b from b3 shot 3 to the end: NO MEDAL, cuffs folded back, belt tucked, seams squared; cap, holster and moustache unchanged. From b4 the wooden revolver is buttoned in the holster. From b5 Nandini's black phone is in his left chest pocket, screen turned inward, only its top edge showing. In the godown (b8) he is a small figure, back to camera; his face is never seen inside.
characters.voice_note: Same actor and voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned small-town north-Indian English, as learnt from manuals ('kindly'): complete sentences, the passive where he can use it, no contractions at all tonight. English police words said with great care. Not British, not American. Courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes. Frightened tonight: a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. Inside the godown (l30, then l16 to l23 and l32) he speaks FULL VOICE and formally to Bhaiyaji, as if reading a register aloud, and never says 'madam'. l23 is read in the same procedural voice until the last word, 'Bhaiyaji', which trails off; l32 follows as a thin, careful question, the first time the procedure fails him.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable, twenty-six years at the Imlipur thana. Tonight her old keypad handset is the listening end of the call and the only place the recording exists.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid, round shoulders. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low on her nose. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar on each teal epaulette, lantern sleeve patches, under an open hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan with two sagging pockets, a ball of orange wool in the right one. Cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder outdoors. Her phone: an old keypad handset in a knitted orange cover. At the stall (b7 to b11) the handset lies face up on the knitting in her lap, screen lit, on speaker. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same actor and voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried small-town Indian English with a clear Hindi accent, short sentences; keeps 'madam' and 'sahab'. Not British, not American. Never surprised; under pressure she gets slower and more exact, and her knitting stops. l02 is an objection she is not allowed to finish. l27, the episode's last line, is level and fully voiced: she reports it like a duty entry.

characters.name: Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur
characters.role: Runs the ration godown and most of Imlipur. Voice only in this episode, heard through Pushpa's handset on speaker.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Same actor and voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice. Soft, hospitable small-town north-Indian English with a Hindi accent; keeps 'Inspector sahab'; his welcome is 'Come in, come in' (l15, echoed in l24). Not British, not American. Courteous to the point of menace; never threatens, never hurries, laughs before he says the worst thing. Through l15 to l21 he is the generous host of every month. l24 is the laugh and the worst thing, close to the phone. In l26 the smile has left his voice: flat and quiet, still fully voiced. Phone-filtered in the mix (narrow band from a keypad loudspeaker), filter wide enough that consonants survive.

location: Three of the seven series plates: talkies_lobby (b1 to b5), crossing_stall (b6, b7, b8 shot 2, b9 to b11), godown exterior (b8 shot 1, and the faceless inserts in b9: tarpaulin and stencil patch required, slip optional). Fictional town of Imlipur, a railway line cutting it in two; the godown's dark front is visible small beyond the track from the crossing. No crowd; Bhaiyaji is never seen.
time_of_day: Night. 11 p.m. in b1 (the held frame of s2e03); a quarter to twelve in b5; a few minutes to twelve at the crossing (b6); midnight to about ten past twelve at the stall (b7 to b11). Clocks are painted with hands and no numerals; no time is spoken.

beats.action: Plate: talkies_lobby, night, one bare bulb. OPENS ON THE HELD FRAME of s2e03 b10 with one change. Shot 1 (insert, 1.0 s silent, the hook): his two wrists held out low over the desk, sleeves over the knuckles, the wooden revolver lying in profile on the desk behind them; her left hand has closed over both wrists and is pushing them down onto the desk; the open handcuffs still hang from her right hand at the top of frame. Shot 2 (insert): the handcuffs going back into the black pouch on her right hip (l01). Shot 3 (two-shot, Nandini picture-left, Pushpa picture-right by the desk end; Nirala only as his sleeves at the frame edge): Pushpa starts to object (l02). Shot 4 (single, Nandini, chest up, level; the cut lands on the dash of l02): she cuts her off, l03. No more than two faces in any frame.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] One more night. My responsibility.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [sharply] Madam, DSP sahab's order. Whoever helps him is named in the same FIR—

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] I heard it, Pushpa ji. The name they write will be mine.

beats.action: Plate: talkies_lobby. She dresses him like an officer of her own force: three single images, one change each. Shot 1 (insert, waist): her hands pulling his black belt tight and tucking the loose tail into the loop; 1.0 s silent (the belt), then l28 begins. Shot 2 (insert, shoulder): her hands squaring a drooping shoulder seam; the edge of the medal's ribbon at frame edge; l28 ends over it. Shot 3 (medium single, Nirala, chest up, standing like a boy being measured, cap dead level, looking down at himself; only her hands in frame, folding back his right cuff so his hand shows; the medal still on his chest): l04, which he says to the uniform as much as to her. Nandini's face is not in this frame.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] You have to face Bhaiyaji as an Inspector.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] For the first time, this uniform fits, madam.

beats.action: Plate: talkies_lobby. Shot 1 (insert, close, Glimpse B image 1): her fingers on the safety pin of the big brass medal on his chest: l05. Shot 2 (single, Nirala, close): he looks stricken, eyes on her hands; 1.0 s silent. Shot 3 (insert): the medal in her fingers going into her own left chest pocket; her thumb buttoning the flap: l06. From this shot on he has no medal.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] In my force, we don't wear a medal like this.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Come back and collect your medal.

beats.action: Plate: talkies_lobby. Shot 1 (insert, strict profile, Glimpse B image 2): the carved teak revolver, pale grain and a knot visible, sliding into the brown leather holster on his right hip; her hand on the flap, buttoning it. 0.8 s silent (leather and wood), then l07 over the same still. Shot 2 (single, Nirala, front on, cap level, cuffs folded back, no medal): l08. The revolver is never pointed at anything.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Don't take the revolver out. Bhaiyaji has a real one.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] I have not taken it out in two years, madam.

beats.action: Plate: talkies_lobby, the wall clock behind them at a quarter to twelve. Shot 1 (insert): Pushpa's old keypad handset in its knitted orange cover, buzzing in her palm; her thumb presses one key. 1.5 s silent (ring, key click, one short beep). Shot 2 (single, Pushpa, level): l09. Shot 3 (insert): Nandini's black smartphone, screen turned inward, sliding into his left chest pocket, just below the two pin holes where the medal was: l29. Shot 4 (two-shot, close, Nandini picture-left, Nirala picture-right, face to face): l10, then l11, a checklist (about 9 s on this frame: S7 holds it on its camera move). Shot 5 (single, Nirala, close, listening; the cut lands on l12): l12 over him, then he repeats the danger word to himself, l13, over the same close. l11 and l12 are separate takes. Pushpa is out of frame from shot 3.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] Recording is on, madam. On my phone.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] My phone stays in your pocket. The call stays on.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Whatever you see, say it aloud. So the witness hears.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] The slip, the sack count, and Bhaiyaji's own voice.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] If there's danger, say: 'The tea has gone cold.'

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] The tea has gone cold.

beats.action: Plate: crossing_stall, a few minutes to twelve. Shot 1 (wide, 1.0 s silent): the red railway signal lamp, the single track across frame, the red-and-white gate arm up, the shut tea stall with its one bulb; three silhouettes at the gate arm (a tall straight one with a round helmet under her left arm, a short square one with needles crossed in her bun, a small one under a level peaked cap); beyond the track the dark road and, small in the distance, the godown's open mouth, a black rectangle with one bulb deep inside. The shutter is UP. Shot 2 (two-shot, side on, Nandini picture-left, Nirala picture-right, one frame): he salutes her and she returns it: l14 over it. Shot 3 (wide still, Glimpse B image 3, held 3.0 s silent after l14): the small figure under the level cap walking alone up the dark road toward the godown mouth, the two women's silhouettes small at the gate arm behind him.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Go ahead, Nirala ji.

beats.action: Plate: crossing_stall, the stall at night, shut, one hanging bulb. Shot 1 (two-shot, front on, the bench under the bulb: Nandini picture-left, notebook open on her knee, the blue pen out over it, red helmet on the bench beside her; Pushpa picture-right, knitting in her lap, the orange keypad handset lying face up on the wool, screen lit, on speaker and muted at this end). 2.0 s silent: his footsteps on gravel through the handset. Then Bhaiyaji's welcome, l15, and Nirala's greeting through the handset, l30 (about 7 s on this one frame). No shutter sound in this beat: the shutter first moves in b8 (D-016 direction 13).

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [chuckles] Come in, come in, Inspector sahab.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Namaskar, Bhaiyaji.

beats.action: Two shots on two plates (D-016 direction 19); Bhaiyaji is not seen. Shot 1 (plate: godown, exterior, wide; Glimpse B image 4): the lit mouth of the godown among stacked jute sacks; the small figure under the peaked cap has stepped just inside, back to camera; the shutter's bottom edge is coming down a hand's height above his cap. The fall is sound: 2.5 s silent of rattle, slam and then a full 1.0 s of nothing. Shot 2 (plate: crossing_stall, the b7 set-up, tighter): both women frozen, Nandini's pen stopped above the page. A second after the rattle dies, his voice through the handset, full voice, formal, to Bhaiyaji: l16. Glimpse B ends on this line.

supers.on_shot: shot 1 (godown exterior, the shutter coming down), held at least 2 s
supers.note: Place super at the godown's first close appearance on path B (viewer ledger places.godown). It sits on shot 1, not on l16's shot 2, because shot 2 is the stall. b8 shot 1 is in Glimpse B: S14 re-cuts against must_not_reveal; a place name reveals nothing on that list.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Why has the shutter been brought down, Bhaiyaji?

beats.action: Plate: crossing_stall (two required faceless inserts and one optional on the godown plate). On the line he does the job, saying aloud everything he sees; Bhaiyaji obliges; for half a minute it is working. Shot 1 (single, Nandini, close, pen moving on the page): l17; on l18, cut to the REQUIRED faceless insert on the godown plate: the truck's grey tarpaulin with sacks to the top. Shot 2 (insert): Pushpa's needles slowing over the lit handset: l19; on l20, cut to the REQUIRED faceless insert on the godown plate: a sack's blank stencil patch under the bulb. Shot 3 (single, Nandini, the shot 1 set-up): l21, then her own murmur as she writes, l22. 0.8 s silent: paper rustling through the handset (he has the slip in his hand). Shot 4 (insert): Nandini's pen stops on the page: l23, then l32 over the same still. OPTIONAL, S7's call if the stall reads static (bible writer_notes): over the 0.8 s rustle a pink slip in a hand with a folded-back khaki cuff, no mark readable. No face inside the godown.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] Big load today, Inspector sahab. Let no eye fall on it.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] The truck is full, Bhaiyaji. Sacks up to the tarpaulin.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] It goes over the crossing tonight itself.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Kindly show me the slip, Bhaiyaji. Eight hundred sacks... government stamped.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [chuckles] All eight hundred. Count them.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Eight hundred. Government. Tonight.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] But SHO sahab has already signed this slip, Bhaiyaji...

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] Then why was I invited here at all?

beats.action: Plate: crossing_stall. REVERSAL. Shot 1 (close, Nandini, eyes on the handset, pen stopped): 1.5 s of silence, a beat too long, then Bhaiyaji's laugh close to the phone and the worst thing, l24, then 1.0 s silent: a loud rustle of cloth against the microphone through the handset, his hand finding the pocket, fully settled before l25. Shot 2 (insert, under the second half of l24 and the rustle after it): Pushpa's needles stopped dead in the wool beside the handset. Shot 3 (close, Nandini, the shot 1 set-up, eyes up from the page): she states the reversal herself, unfiltered, l25, then l31 over the same close.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [laughs] Fake Inspector! Come in... it's you I was waiting for.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Bhaiyaji knew.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] The invitation was a trap.

beats.action: Plate: crossing_stall. ENDING, SPOKEN. Shot 1 (insert, close): the orange handset on the wool; Bhaiyaji right on top of the phone: l26. Shot 2 (medium, Nandini on her feet beside the bench, her left hand flat over her buttoned left chest pocket where the medal is; Pushpa still seated below her, looking up): the flat tone of a dead line, 1.0 s silent. Shot 3 (insert, close): the handset's screen gone dark on the wool: l27 over it, then 1.5 s held in silence. Silence in b11 is 2.5 s in all.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [quietly] And whose phone is this, in your pocket?

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] Madam... the line has gone dead.

sfx_notes: Bed b1 to b5 (series talkies_lobby night ambience, shared with s2e03): hum of one bare bulb, crickets outside the open lobby doors, a slow wall-clock tick. Nothing in it is loud.

b1: under the 1.0 s opening, a soft slap of her palm closing on his wrists against wood; then the cuffs' chain chinking once as they drop into the leather pouch, and the pouch flap snapping shut, before l01 ends.
b2: leather belt pulled tight through its buckle; stiff starched cloth creasing; a cuff folded back. Close and small.
b3: the tiny metallic click of the safety pin opening (in the 1.0 s hold); a button pushed through a pocket flap under l06.
b4: wood sliding into leather, a dry hollow sound, not metal; the holster flap's press-stud closing, then l07.

b5: two soft taps on a smartphone screen; Pushpa's keypad handset rings once (shared series keypad tone, monophonic), cut by a key click and one short high beep as recording starts; then l09. Under l29 the smartphone slides into cloth.

b6: crossing night bed, wider and emptier than the lobby: crickets, a far dog, the faint buzz of the signal lamp. No train anywhere in this episode. Under the 3.0 s hold after l14, his footsteps on gravel walking away and fading.
Bed b7 to b11 (crossing_stall night): one bulb's hum, crickets, very low. Pushpa's needles click softly from b7 until they slow in b9 and stop in b10.

Phone voices b7 to b11: Bhaiyaji and Nirala come only through Pushpa's handset loudspeaker on the wool: narrow band, a little godown echo (tin roof, a big hollow shed), filter wide enough that every consonant survives. His footsteps on gravel in b7 come through the same filter.

b8 shot 1: the shutter rattling down, heard live and far across the track (not through the phone), ending in one slam; the rattle must be completely dead a full second before l16. l16 is through the handset. Bed ducks under l16.
b9: before l23, paper rustling close to the hidden phone (0.8 s), through the filter. Keep it short and soft so l23 does not sit on it.

b10: the 1.5 s before l24 is near-silence: bulb hum only, the needles already slowing. Bhaiyaji's laugh is close to the microphone; let it distort a little but never let it mask the words of l24. The needles stop on the laugh. Bed ducks right down under l25 (unfiltered, at the stall). After l24, a loud cloth rustle against the microphone (his hand finding the pocket), 1.0 s, through the filter, settled before l25; the bed ducks under l25.

b11: l26 through the filter, close and dry, with no effect under it or just before it. Then the flat continuous tone of a dead line from the handset for 1.0 s; it drops to near silence under l27 so the cliffhanger line is fully clear, and returns faintly in the 1.5 s hold before cut to black.
music_note: No music in b1 to b4: the dressing is played in room tone so the small sounds of belt, pin and holster carry it. From b5 a single low sustained string note, barely audible, under the wiring; it holds through the salute and the walk in b6 and fades out as the footsteps fade. b7 to b9: no music at all; the phone and the stall carry it, so the sting sounds real. On the laugh in b10, one soft low note enters, ducked under l24 and l25, and holds through b11 under the dead tone; it is cut to silence on the last frame. Instrumental, no melody, no percussion hits, no sting on the reversal.
ending_question: Bhaiyaji was waiting for a fake Inspector and has now found Nandini's phone in his pocket: what will he do with Nirala, and how will Nandini reach him with no order, no force and a dead line?
writer_notes: English adaptation of script.hi.json (S5), not a literal translation. Same beats, same speakers, same order and the same line ids (l01 to l32; l28 to l31 added in the D-024 pass and l32 in the C1 fix round, in both files); same silent_seconds per beat and the same silence positions as the Hindi writer_notes give ('Format'; since the critic rerun's must-fix, b10 is 1.5 s before l24 and 1.0 s of cloth rustle between l24 and l25, and b11 is 1.0 s between l26 and l27 and 1.5 s after l27). action, on_screen, location, time_of_day, sfx_notes and music_note are copied unchanged, because picture, sound and music are shared between the two cuts. The Hindi notes on format, recording logic, Glimpse B, faces per frame, continuity and plates are production notes and apply to this cut unchanged; they are not repeated here. In the character blocks only name and voice_note change, and Nirala's role says 'Inspector sahab' in Latin script.

Sources: content/series2/episodes/s2b01/script.hi.json; content/series2/bible.json per-character English registers and sample lines (Nandini neutral educated Indian English keeping 'madam' and 'ji'; Nirala manual English, 'kindly', no contractions when nervous; Pushpa plain, short sentences, keeps 'madam', 'SHO sahab', 'Nirala ji'; Bhaiyaji soft and hospitable, keeps 'Inspector sahab' and 'aaiye', though this cut drops 'aaiye' since the C1 fix round); content/proof/photoreal/script.en.json for format; docs/decisions.md D-006 change 13, D-016 directions 4, 7, 12 and 13, D-014.

Register choices. Nirala never contracts ('I have not taken it out', 'Why has the shutter been brought down', passive as in his Hindi), and l20 carries his 'kindly'. 'Show me the slip' replaces 'give the slip', which in English means to escape. Nandini and Bhaiyaji may contract. 'Tonight itself' (l19) and 'Let no eye fall on it' (l17, the Hindi 'नज़र ना लगे', both the evil eye and 'nobody must see this', which is why the shutter came down) are kept as Indian English idiom. 'Come in' opens l15 and returns in l24, so the laugh lands as an echo of the welcome, as 'आइए' does in the Hindi (until the C1 fix round this was an untranslated 'Aaiye'; C1 series2-B-en flagged it). l27 is 'the line has gone dead' (critic rerun, optional item, taken), not 'the line is cut', which reads as a translation; it is written uncontracted so it stays clear under the dead tone, same tag and target.

Fixed wording that later episodes must reuse: the danger phrase is 'The tea has gone cold.' (l12, l13; it pays off in s2b02 b3). Nirala says it with no contraction, so it is written that way in Nandini's line too. The S5 pass on s2b02 should use these exact words. l24 is also fixed wording: s2b03 en l12 quotes it word for word as the recorded evidence (D-006 change 11), dropping only 'Come in...' (formerly 'Aaiye...') as the Hindi drops 'आइए', so it reads 'Fake Inspector! It's you I was waiting for.' The C1 round changed only that dropped word, so s2b03 en l12's text still quotes l24 word for word; only s2b03's writer note that cites the old 'Aaiye...' is stale. Do not reword l24 without changing s2b03 en l12 (and its b6 action cue and writer_notes) in the same pass. 'It's you' keeps the stress of 'आप ही का': Bhaiyaji expected this impostor, which is what l25 'Bhaiyaji knew.' rests on. l05 keeps D-016 direction 12's sense ('In my force') without a gendered word, which English does not need.

Under D-019 silences are shortened first, and the line-trim order fires only on D-019's two-episode trigger; until then nothing is trimmed.
